distractors.reason: 'Hardly' means 'almost not' or 'barely', so 'work hardly' means working very little, the opposite of the intended meaning.
We don't say 'work heavily' in standard English. 'Heavily' is used with things like 'rain heavily' or 'rely heavily'.
We don't say 'work strictly'. 'Strictly' describes following rules, as in 'strictly forbidden'.

example_sentence: Teenagers who take summer jobs often work ___ to save money.
l1_interference: Носії української мови іноді ставлять прислівник перед дієсловом або плутають 'hard' з 'hardly', тому можуть сказати 'work hardly' замість правильного 'work hard'.
explanation: In English, the adverb 'hard' follows the verb 'work' to describe the effort put into an action. Its meaning is 'with great effort', which is different from 'hardly'.

related_collocations.example: Many students work part-time during the school year.
She volunteers regularly at the local animal shelter.
Please listen carefully to the instructions.

memory_tip: HARD = with great effort (work hard, study hard) | HARDLY = almost not (hardly ever, hardly any)
